name: Command Sent, Never Confirmed
description: The point simple systems forget: a command is not the same thing as its execution. A close command goes out, feedback never comes back, the real command-supervision timeout elapses, and the system reports it - the device is never shown as closed.

steps.description: Close command issued for a demo breaker whose feedback never arrives - watch it sit in FEEDBACK_PENDING (command_status). Goes through the exact same real dispatch path as every other command step - nothing here is faked except that this one device's feedback is intentionally never wired up.

steps.message: Command supervision timeout: the breaker did not confirm its commanded state within 2.5 s
steps.description: The real 2.5 s command-supervision timeout (CommandManager's own timeout_ms) has elapsed - command_status is TIMEOUT. The system reports the failure; at no point did the breaker's own displayed state show CLOSED, because it never actually confirmed.
Clears when you're done showing the point
